items.title: Oil dips as Iran agrees to join U.S. peace talks in Islamabad

featured_image.name: US-Iran direct talks on ending war under way in Pakistan

items.description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday as expectations grew that the United States and Iran would resume peace negotiations in Pakistan this week, raising hopes for an easing of supply disruptions in the Middle East. The decline came after a volatile Monday session that saw crude surge on renewed tensions over the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Clean energy outpaced global electricity demand growth in 2025, Ember finds

featured_image.name: The State of Clean Energy, in 10 Charts - World Resources Institute

items.description:
Clean energy generation outpaced global electricity demand growth for the first time in 2025, powered by record solar expansion in China and India, according to energy think tank Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026, released on Monday.[1][2]

Clean power generation grew 887 terawatt hours last year, exceeding overall global electricity demand growth of 849 terawatt hours, the report found. Solar energy, which grew 30% in 2025, alone met three-quarters of the net rise in electricity demand, and combined with wind power generation, met 99% of it.[3][1]

items.title: Asian markets trade mixed as U.S.-Iran ceasefire set to expire Tuesday night

featured_image.name: Asian markets track Wall St down with Nvidia, US jobs in view

items.description:
Oil prices dipped and Asian stock markets traded in mixed fashion on Tuesday as uncertainty deepened over the fate of peace negotiations between the United States and Iran, with a two-week ceasefire set to expire Tuesday evening Eastern time.

Brent crude slipped 0.4% while U.S. benchmark crude fell 0.9% in early Asian trading, according to the Associated Press. The declines came as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic talks in Islamabad against rising tensions, including the U.S. Navy's recent seizure of an Iranian cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Oil prices surge as US-Iran ceasefire nears expiration

featured_image.name: Oil prices surge amid mixed signals on US-Iran peace talks

items.description: Oil prices swung sharply on Monday as escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz collided with uncertainty over whether the United States and Iran would sit down for a second round of peace talks before a ceasefire expires on Wednesday.

items.title: Iran warns of 'new cards on the battlefield' as ceasefire nears end

featured_image.name: Who Is Mohammed-Baqer Qalibaf?

items.description: Iran's Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf declared on Monday that Tehran will not negotiate with the United States under coercion, accusing President Donald Trump of trying to turn the negotiating table into "a table of surrender." His remarks came as the ceasefire between the two countries neared its expiration and uncertainty mounted over whether a second round of peace talks would take place.

items.title: Iran warns of 'new cards on the battlefield' as ceasefire nears expiration

featured_image.name: No date set for US-Iran talks, as Pakistan pushes to keep diplomacy ...

items.description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned on Monday that Tehran has prepared to "reveal new cards on the battlefield" if war with the United States resumes, as a two-week ceasefire approaches its Wednesday expiration with no deal in sight and negotiations in disarray.

items.title: LHC experiment finds high-significance crack in the Standard Model

featured_image.name: Our Large Hadron Collider results hint at undiscovered physics

items.description: Physicists working on the Large Hadron Collider at CERN in Geneva have reported a measurement that deviates from the predictions of the Standard Model of particle physics by four standard deviations — a result that, if confirmed, could represent the first crack in the theory that has dominated the field for half a century.

items.title: Iraq, Syria reopen Rabia border crossing after 13 years

featured_image.name: IRAQ-SYRIA-DIPLOMACY-TRADE-BORDER

items.description: Iraq and Syria on Monday officially reopened the Rabia-Al Yarubiyah border crossing, restoring a trade and transit route that had been shuttered for nearly 13 years amid civil war and the rise of ISIS. The reopening makes all official border crossings between the two countries operational for the first time since conflict engulfed the region.

items.title: Apple names John Ternus CEO as Tim Cook shifts to chairman role

featured_image.name: Apple (AAPL) Names John Ternus as Next CEO, With Tim Cook ...

items.description:
Apple announced on Monday that John Ternus, the company's senior vice president of hardware engineering, will become its next chief executive officer effective September 1, replacing Tim Cook, who will transition to the role of executive chairman of the board. The move, approved unanimously by Apple's board of directors, caps months of intensifying succession speculation and marks only the third CEO transition in Apple's 50-year history.[1][2][3][4]

Cook will remain as CEO through the summer to work closely with Ternus on the handover. As executive chairman, Cook will continue to assist the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world. Arthur Levinson, Apple's non-executive chairman for the past 15 years, will become the board's lead independent director on the same date.[3][1]

items.title: Starmer admits misleading Parliament over Mandelson vetting scandal

featured_image.name: Britain's Starmer Admits Misleading Parliament Over ...

items.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer addressed a hostile House of Commons on Monday, admitting that he had misled Parliament over the failed security vetting of Lord Peter Mandelson — but insisted the error was inadvertent.[1][2][3]

Starmer told lawmakers he should never have appointed Mandelson as the United Kingdom's ambassador to Washington, acknowledging a catastrophic lapse that has now engulfed his premiership and drawn resignation calls from all major opposition parties.[4][5]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon to hold second round of talks in Washington on Thursday

featured_image.name: Rare Israel–Lebanon direct talks hosted by top US diplomat ...

items.description:
Israel and Lebanon are set to hold a second round of ambassador-level talks in Washington on Thursday, April 23, according to Israeli media reports, marking the first direct diplomatic contact between the two countries since a 10-day ceasefire took effect on April 16.[1][2][3]

The meeting, expected to be hosted at the U.S. State Department, follows a first round held on April 14 that was widely described as historic — the highest-level direct engagement between Israel and Lebanon since 1993. That session, chaired by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, lasted more than two hours and included Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter, Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad, and other U.S. officials.[4][5][6]

items.title: Starmer to face Commons over Mandelson vetting scandal

featured_image.name: UK PM Starmer's authority tested as domestic struggles ...

items.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is set to address the House of Commons on Monday in what is being described as a fight for his political survival, as he seeks to explain how Peter Mandelson was appointed as ambassador to the United States despite having failed security vetting — a fact Starmer insists was concealed from him by Foreign Office officials.

items.title: Atomic clocks could reveal time flowing at multiple speeds, physicists say

featured_image.name: US scientists show time can go quantum in ion clock experiments

items.description: A team of physicists has shown that cutting-edge atomic clocks may be capable of detecting a long-predicted but never-observed quantum effect: time itself existing in superposition, flowing at multiple rates at once. The research, published on April 20 in Physical Review Letters, outlines how trapped-ion clocks could soon test whether a single clock can experience different passages of time simultaneously — a phenomenon the authors liken to a "quantum twin paradox."[1][2]

items.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire extension 'highly unlikely' as talks falter

featured_image.name: U.S. Seizes Iranian Cargo Ship Amid Peace Talk Standoff

items.description: President Donald Trump said Monday it is "highly unlikely" he will extend the two-week ceasefire with Iran if no agreement is reached before it expires on Wednesday, warning that military strikes on bridges and power plants could follow and that the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz will remain in place until a deal is signed.[1][2]

items.title: Iran signals possible return to US talks after initial rejection

featured_image.name: Failed U.S.-Iran negotiations in Pakistan raise questions ... - PBS

items.description: The prospect of a second round of US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad swung between collapse and cautious revival on Monday as Tehran initially rejected participation, only to signal later in the day that it was "positively reviewing" a return to the negotiating table, according to a senior Iranian official who spoke to Reuters. The diplomatic whiplash came just two days before a fragile ceasefire between the two sides is set to expire on Wednesday, April 22.[1][2][3]

items.title: White House says US ready to back UAE financially amid Iran war

featured_image.name: UAE asks US for a wartime financial lifeline | MEO

items.description:
White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett confirmed on Monday that the United States is prepared to provide financial assistance to the United Arab Emirates should the ongoing war with Iran further damage the Gulf state's economic outlook, though he indicated Washington does not expect such a step will be necessary.[1]

The remarks follow a report by The Wall Street Journal that UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the prospect of establishing a currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and officials from the Federal Reserve during meetings in Washington last week. No formal request for a swap line has been submitted, and Emirati representatives framed the discussions as a "preliminary and precautionary measure".[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Trump to consider lifting Hormuz blockade after Pakistan army chief's call

featured_image.name: U.S. Seizes Iranian Cargo Ship Amid Peace Talk Standoff

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump told Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir in a phone call that he would consider his advice on lifting the Strait of Hormuz naval blockade, a Pakistani security source said on Monday, in a development that could open a path to resuming stalled peace talks with Iran as a ceasefire nears expiration.[1][2]

The exchange came as a U.S. delegation was set to travel to Islamabad on Monday for a second round of Pakistan-brokered negotiations, though Tehran has not confirmed whether it will attend.[3][4]

items.title: Fungus from NASA cleanrooms survived simulated Mars trip

featured_image.name: Fungi may survive extreme conditions of Mars and space, say ...

items.description:
A fungus found lurking in NASA's ultra-clean spacecraft assembly rooms could withstand the punishing conditions of a trip to Mars and persist on the planet's surface, according to new research that raises fresh questions about keeping other worlds free from Earth's biology.

The study, published this week in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, is the first to demonstrate that a microbial eukaryote — a complex, nucleus-bearing organism — could survive every phase of a Mars mission, from pre-launch preparation through space travel to robotic surface exploration.[1][2]

items.title: UK pushes for toll-free Hormuz as ceasefire nears expiry

featured_image.name: UK's Cooper urges full resumption of shipping through Hormuz Strait

items.description: Britain's Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper has intensified diplomatic efforts to secure unrestricted navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, warning that the waterway must reopen fully and without tolls as the fragile US-Iran ceasefire teeters on the brink of collapse.

items.title: Iran pulls out of US talks after ship seizure

featured_image.name: Iran says no talks with US for now, casting doubt over Pakistan efforts

items.description:
The United States military fired on and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, the first known use of force in Washington's naval blockade of Iranian ports, throwing a fragile ceasefire into crisis less than 48 hours before it is set to expire.

U.S. Central Command said the guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance intercepted the Touska, a 294-meter cargo vessel, as it sailed through the Arabian Sea toward the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. After the crew ignored repeated warnings, the warship used its deck gun to disable the vessel's engine room, and Marines from the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit boarded from helicopters launched off the amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli.[1][2][3]

President Donald Trump announced the seizure on Truth Social, writing that the ship had been "stopped right in its tracks by a hole in the engine room" and that Marines had taken control. The Touska and its owners were already under U.S. Treasury sanctions for allegedly helping Iran evade trade restrictions.[2][1]
